convert this recipe:

Pad Thai (serves 2)

8 oz rice noodles
2 tbsp tamarind paste
2 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp palm sugar
1 tbsp lime juice
200g shrimp, deveined
2 eggs
1 cup bean sprouts
3 green onions, sliced
1/4 cup roasted peanuts, crushed
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp vegetable oil

Soak noodles in warm water for 30 minutes until pliable. Drain.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice to make the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds.
Add shrimp, cook 2 minutes until pink. Push to the side.
Crack eggs into the wok, scramble them.
Add noodles and sauce, toss everything together for 2-3 minutes.
Add bean sprouts and green onions, toss for 30 seconds.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts and a lime wedge.

hey can you add this recipe? it's from my grandmother:

Beef bourguignon

You need about 1kg of beef chuck cut into large cubes. Season with salt and pepper. In a large dutch oven, brown the beef in batches in some oil, then set aside. In the same pot, cook 200g of lardons until crispy. Add 2 diced carrots, 2 stalks of celery chopped, and 1 large onion diced. Cook for about 5 minutes. Add 4 cloves of garlic and cook another minute. Pour in a whole bottle of red wine (750ml) and 2 cups of beef stock. Add a bouquet garni (thyme, bay leaves, parsley stems), 2 tablespoons of tomato paste. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Return the beef to the pot. Cover and cook in the oven at 160°C for about 3 hours. In the last 30 minutes, add 250g of pearl onions and 300g of cremini mushrooms that you've sautéed in butter. Adjust seasoning and serve with crusty bread.

evals.prompt:
Japanese Milk Bread

Tangzhong:
25g bread flour
120ml whole milk

Dough:
375g bread flour
50g sugar
7g salt
7g instant yeast
120ml whole milk (warm)
1 large egg
55g unsalted butter (softened)

Egg wash: 1 egg + 1 tbsp milk

Make tangzhong: whisk flour and milk in small saucepan over medium heat until thick paste forms (about 3 min). Cool to room temp.

In stand mixer with dough hook, combine flour, sugar, salt, yeast. Add warm milk, egg, and cooled tangzhong. Mix on low 2 min then medium 5 min. Add butter piece by piece, knead 10 min until windowpane.

Bulk ferment 1 hour covered until doubled. Punch down, divide into 4 pieces. Shape into balls, rest 15 min. Roll each into oval, fold in thirds like a letter. Roll into tight cylinder. Place in greased 9x5 loaf pan.

Final proof 45 min until dough rises 1 inch above pan rim. Brush with egg wash.

Bake 350°F (175°C) for 30-35 minutes until deep golden. Internal temp 190°F.

Cool 10 min in pan, then unmold onto wire rack.
